## List all fees

<a id="opIdfindAllFees"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/fees \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /fees`

This endpoint is used for retrieving all fees that have been issued.

<h3 id="list-all-fees-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number. Defaults to 1. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records per page. Defaults to 100. The maximum is 200, unless another maximum is configured for your organization. A value above the maximum returns a `422` error with `value_is_out_of_range` on `per_page`. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the default number of records.|
|external_customer_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier assigned to the customer in your application.|
|external_subscription_id|query|string|false|External subscription ID|
|event_transaction_id|query|string|false|Filter results by event transaction ID|
|currency|query|object|false|Filter results by the fee's currency.|
|fee_type|query|string|false|The fee type. Possible values are `add_on`, `charge`, `fixed_charge`, `credit`, `subscription` or `commitment`.|
|billable_metric_code|query|string|false|Filter results by the `code` of the billable metric attached to the fee. Only applies to `charge` types.|
|payment_status|query|string|false|Indicates the payment status of the fee. It represents the current status of the payment associated with the fee. The possible values for this field are `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed` and `refunded`.|
|created_at_from|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results created at or after this date and time in UTC.|
|created_at_to|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results created at or before this date and time in UTC.|
|succeeded_at_from|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment success at or after this date and time in UTC.|
|succeeded_at_to|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment success at or before this date and time in UTC.|
|failed_at_from|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment failure at or after this date and time in UTC.|
|failed_at_to|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment failure at or before this date and time in UTC.|
|refunded_at_from|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment refund at or after this date and time in UTC.|
|refunded_at_to|query|string(date-time)|false|Filter results with a payment refund at or before this date and time in UTC.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|fee_type|charge|
|fee_type|fixed_charge|
|fee_type|add_on|
|fee_type|subscription|
|fee_type|credit|
|fee_type|commitment|
|payment_status|pending|
|payment_status|succeeded|
|payment_status|failed|
|payment_status|refunded|

## Update a fee

<a id="opIdupdateFee"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/fees/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "fee": {
      "payment_status": "succeeded"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /fees/{lago_id}`

This endpoint is used for updating the payment status of a specific fee. Only a fee that is not attached to an invoice can be updated; once the fee is on an invoice, its payment status follows the invoice and the endpoint returns a `405` error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "fee": {
    "payment_status": "succeeded"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-fee-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the fee within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the fee's record within the Lago system.|
|body|body|[FeeUpdateInput](#schemafeeupdateinput)|true|Fee payload|
|» fee|body|object|true|none|
|» » payment_status|body|string|true|The payment status of the fee. Possible values are `pending`, `succeeded`, `failed` or `refunded`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » payment_status|pending|
|» » payment_status|succeeded|
|» » payment_status|failed|
|» » payment_status|refunded|

<h1 id="lago-api-documentation-invoices">invoices</h1>

Everything about Invoice collection

<a href="https://getlago.com/docs/api-reference/invoices/invoice-object">Find out more</a>

## List all invoices

<a id="opIdfindAllInvoices"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /invoices`

This endpoint is used for retrieving all invoices.

<h3 id="list-all-invoices-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number. Defaults to 1. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records per page. Defaults to 100. The maximum is 200, unless another maximum is configured for your organization. A value above the maximum returns a `422` error with `value_is_out_of_range` on `per_page`. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the default number of records.|
|external_customer_id|query|string|false|Unique identifier assigned to the customer in your application.|
|amount_from|query|integer|false|Filter invoices of at least a specific amount. This parameter must be defined in cents to ensure consistent handling for all currency types.|
|amount_to|query|integer|false|Filter invoices up to a specific amount. This parameter must be defined in cents to ensure consistent handling for all currency types.|
|issuing_date_from|query|string(date)|false|Filter invoices starting from a specific date.|
|issuing_date_to|query|string(date)|false|Filter invoices up to a specific date.|
|status|query|string|false|Filter invoices by status. Possible values are `draft`, `failed`, `finalized`, `pending` and `voided`.|
|statuses[]|query|[string]|false|Filter invoices by statuses. Possible values are `draft`, `failed`, `finalized`, `pending` and `voided`.|
|payment_status|query|string|false|Filter invoices by payment status. Possible values are `pending`, `failed` or `succeeded`.|
|payment_statuses[]|query|[string]|false|Filter invoices by payment statuses. Possible values are `pending`, `failed` or `succeeded`.|
|payment_overdue|query|boolean|false|Filter invoices by payment_overdue. Possible values are `true` or `false`.|
|search_term|query|string|false|Search invoices by id, number, purchase order number, or by the name, legal name, first name, last name, external_id or email of the customer.|
|currency|query|string|false|Filter invoices by currency. Possible values ISO 4217 currency codes.|
|payment_dispute_lost|query|boolean|false|Filter invoices with a payment dispute lost. Possible values are `true` or `false`.|
|partially_paid|query|boolean|false|Filter invoices that are partially paid. When `true`, only invoices with a non-zero amount paid that is below the total due are returned. When `false`, those invoices are excluded.|
|settlements[]|query|[string]|false|Filter invoices settled by at least one of the given settlement types. `payment` matches invoices settled by a payment, `credit_note` matches invoices settled by a credit note.|
|invoice_type|query|string|false|Filter invoices by invoice type. Possible values are `subscription`, `add_on`, `credit`, `one_off`, `advance_charges` or `progressive_billing`.|
|self_billed|query|boolean|false|Filter invoices by self billed. Possible values are `true` or `false`.|
|billing_entity_codes[]|query|[string]|false|Filter invoices by billing entity codes. Possible values are the billing entity codes you have created.|
|metadata[key]|query|string|false|Filter invoices by metadata. Replace `key` with the actual metadata key you want to match, and provide the corresponding value. Providing empty value will search for invoice without given metadata key. For example, `metadata[color]=blue`.|
|purchase_order_number|query|string|false|Filter by the invoice purchase order number. The match is exact but case-insensitive.|

## Create a one-off invoice

<a id="opIdcreateInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "invoice": {
      "external_customer_id": "hooli_1234",
      "billing_entity_code": "default",
      "currency": "EUR",
      "skip_psp": true,
      "purchase_order_number": "PO-123",
      "fees": [
        {
          "add_on_code": "setup_fee",
          "invoice_display_name": "Setup Fee (SF1)",
          "unit_amount_cents": 12000,
          "units": "2.5",
          "description": "Onboarding session, June 2024",
          "from_datetime": "2022-08-08T00:00:00Z",
          "to_datetime": "2022-08-08T00:00:00Z",
          "tax_codes": [
            "french_standard_vat"
          ]
        }
      ],
      "invoice_custom_section": {
        "skip_invoice_custom_sections": false,
        "invoice_custom_section_codes": [
          "eu_bank_details"
        ]
      },
      "payment_method": {
        "payment_method_type": "provider",
        "payment_method_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90"
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /invoices`

This endpoint is used for issuing a one-off invoice.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "invoice": {
    "external_customer_id": "hooli_1234",
    "billing_entity_code": "default",
    "currency": "EUR",
    "skip_psp": true,
    "purchase_order_number": "PO-123",
    "fees": [
      {
        "add_on_code": "setup_fee",
        "invoice_display_name": "Setup Fee (SF1)",
        "unit_amount_cents": 12000,
        "units": "2.5",
        "description": "Onboarding session, June 2024",
        "from_datetime": "2022-08-08T00:00:00Z",
        "to_datetime": "2022-08-08T00:00:00Z",
        "tax_codes": [
          "french_standard_vat"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "invoice_custom_section": {
      "skip_invoice_custom_sections": false,
      "invoice_custom_section_codes": [
        "eu_bank_details"
      ]
    },
    "payment_method": {
      "payment_method_type": "provider",
      "payment_method_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90"
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-one-off-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvoiceOneOffCreateInput](#schemainvoiceoneoffcreateinput)|true|Invoice payload|
|» invoice|body|object|true|none|
|» » external_customer_id|body|string|true|Unique identifier assigned to the customer in your application.|
|» » billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity to issue the invoice from. If not provided, the customer's billing entity is used.|
|» » currency|body|[Currency](#schemacurrency)|false|The currency of the invoice.|
|» » skip_psp|body|boolean \| null|false|If true, the invoice will be created but not sent to the payment provider.|
|» » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number to associate with the invoice.|
|» » fees|body|[object]|true|none|
|» » » add_on_code|body|string|true|The code of the add-on used as invoice item.|
|» » » invoice_display_name|body|string|false|Specifies the name that will be displayed on an invoice. If no value is set for this field, the name of the actual charge will be used as the default display name.|
|» » » unit_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The amount of the fee per unit, expressed in cents. By default, the amount of the add-on is used.|
|» » » units|body|string \| number \| null|false|The quantity of units associated with the fee. Accepts a number or a decimal string. By default, only 1 unit is added to the invoice.|
|» » » description|body|string \| null|false|The description of the fee line item in the invoice. By default, the description of the add-on is used.|
|» » » from_datetime|body|string(date-time)|false|The lower boundary of the invoice billing interval. The `from_datetime` should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » to_datetime|body|string(date-time)|false|The upper boundary of the invoice billing interval. The `to_datetime` should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » tax_codes|body|[TaxCodes](#schemataxcodes)|false|List of unique code used to identify the taxes.|
|» » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing the invoice payment.|

<h3 id="create-a-one-off-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice created|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request error|[ApiErrorBadRequest](#schemaapierrorbadrequest)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity error|[ApiErrorUnprocessableEntity](#schemaapierrorunprocessableentity)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve an invoice

<a id="opIdfindInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /invoices/{lago_id}`

This endpoint is used for retrieving a specific invoice that has been issued.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Update an invoice

<a id="opIdupdateInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "invoice": {
      "payment_status": "succeeded",
      "metadata": [
        {
          "id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90",
          "key": "digital_ref_id",
          "value": "INV-0123456-98765"
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /invoices/{lago_id}`

This endpoint is used for updating an existing invoice. A voided invoice cannot be updated and returns a `405` error.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "invoice": {
    "payment_status": "succeeded",
    "metadata": [
      {
        "id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90",
        "key": "digital_ref_id",
        "value": "INV-0123456-98765"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|
|body|body|[InvoiceUpdateInput](#schemainvoiceupdateinput)|true|Update an existing invoice|
|» invoice|body|object|true|none|
|» » payment_status|body|string|false|The payment status of the invoice. Possible values are `pending`, `failed` or `succeeded`.|
|» » metadata|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » id|body|string(uuid)|false|The metadata object identifier. Only required when updating existing metadata.|
|» » » key|body|string|false|The key in the key-value pair of the metadata.|
|» » » value|body|string|false|The value in the key-value pair of the metadata (140 characters max).|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » payment_status|pending|
|» » payment_status|succeeded|
|» » payment_status|failed|

## Delete a draft invoice

<a id="opIddeleteInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /invoices/{lago_id}`

This endpoint is used for permanently deleting a `draft` invoice. Deleting a draft invoice removes it entirely: it never becomes accounts receivable, consumes no invoice number, and disappears from every list, export, and analytics surface. Only invoices in the `draft` status can be deleted; for a `finalized` invoice, void it instead.

<h3 id="delete-a-draft-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

<h3 id="delete-a-draft-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice deleted|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Not Allowed error|[ApiErrorNotAllowed](#schemaapierrornotallowed)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Download an invoice PDF

<a id="opIddownloadInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/download \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/download`

This endpoint is used for downloading a specific invoice PDF document. Only `finalized` invoices can be downloaded; any other invoice returns a `404` error.
When the PDF has already been generated, the invoice object is returned and its `file_url` points to the document. When it has not been generated yet, the response is a `200` with an empty body and the generation starts in the background. Call the endpoint again to get the invoice object with its `file_url`.

<h3 id="download-an-invoice-pdf-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

## Finalize a draft invoice

<a id="opIdfinalizeInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/finalize \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /invoices/{lago_id}/finalize`

This endpoint is used for finalizing a draft invoice.

<h3 id="finalize-a-draft-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

## Mark an invoice payment dispute as lost

<a id="opIdloseDisputeInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/lose_dispute \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/lose_dispute`

This endpoint is used for setting invoice's payment dispute as lost.

<h3 id="mark-an-invoice-payment-dispute-as-lost-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice payment dispute lost|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Not Allowed error|[ApiErrorNotAllowed](#schemaapierrornotallowed)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Refresh a draft invoice

<a id="opIdrefreshInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/refresh \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`PUT /invoices/{lago_id}/refresh`

This endpoint is used for refreshing a draft invoice.

<h3 id="refresh-a-draft-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

<h3 id="refresh-a-draft-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice refreshed|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|[ApiErrorForbidden](#schemaapierrorforbidden)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Retry generation of a failed invoice

<a id="opIdretryInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/retry \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/retry`

This endpoint is used for retrying to generate a failed invoice.

<h3 id="retry-generation-of-a-failed-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

<h3 id="retry-generation-of-a-failed-invoice-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice generation has been retried|[Invoice](#schemainvoice)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|

bearerAuth

## Generate a payment URL

<a id="opIdinvoicePaymentUrl"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/payment_url \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/payment_url`

This endpoint generates a checkout link for a specific invoice.

<h3 id="generate-a-payment-url-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "invoice_payment_details": {
    "lago_customer_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90",
    "lago_invoice_id": "1e501a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a80",
    "external_customer_id": "5eb02857-a71e-4ea2-bcf9-57d3a41bc6ba",
    "payment_provider": "stripe",
    "payment_url": "https://foo.bar"
  }
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "status": 401,
  "error": "Unauthorized"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "status": 404,
  "error": "Not Found",
  "code": "object_not_found"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "status": 422,
  "error": "Unprocessable entity",
  "code": "validation_errors",
  "error_details": {}
}
```

<h3 id="generate-a-payment-url-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Payment URL has been generated|[InvoicePaymentUrl](#schemainvoicepaymenturl)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable entity error|[ApiErrorUnprocessableEntity](#schemaapierrorunprocessableentity)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/preview \

    "customer": {

      },
      "state": "CA",

    },

      {
```

This endpoint is used for generating invoice preview.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "customer": {

    }

  },

```

<h3 id="create-an-invoice-preview-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[InvoicePreviewInput](#schemainvoicepreviewinput)|true|Invoice preview payload|
|» customer|body|object|true|none|
|» » address_line1|body|string|false|The first line of the billing address|
|» » address_line2|body|string \| null|false|The second line of the billing address|
|» » city|body|string|false|The city of the customer's billing address|
|» » country|body|[Country](#schemacountry)|false|Country code of the customer's billing address. Format must be ISO 3166 (alpha-2)|
|» » external_id|body|string|false|Unique identifier assigned to the customer in your application.|
|» » integration_customers|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » integration_type|body|string|true|The integration type used for accounting, tax and CRM syncs.<br>Accepted values: `anrok`, `avalara`, `xero`, `hubspot`, `salesforce`.|
|» » » integration_code|body|string|true|Unique code used to identify an integration connection.|
|» » name|body|string|false|The full name of the customer|
|» » currency|body|[Currency](#schemacurrency)|false|The currency of the invoice.|
|» » shipping_address|body|[Address](#schemaaddress)|false|The shipping address of the customer.|
|» » state|body|string|false|The state of the customer's billing address|
|» » zipcode|body|string|false|The zipcode of the customer's billing address.|
|» » tax_identification_number|body|string|false|The tax identification number of the customer|
|» » timezone|body|[Timezone](#schematimezone)|false|The customer's timezone, used for billing purposes in their local time. Overrides the organization's timezone|
|» plan_code|body|string|false|The code of the plan. It serves as a unique identifier associated with a particular plan. The code is typically used for internal or system-level identification purposes, like assigning a subscription, for instance.|
|» subscription_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The anniversary date and time of the initial subscription. This date serves as the basis for billing subscriptions with `anniversary` billing time. The `anniversary_date` should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» billing_time|body|string|false|The billing time for the subscription, which can be set as either `anniversary` or `calendar`. If not explicitly provided, it will default to `calendar`. The billing time determines the timing of recurring billing cycles for the subscription. By specifying `anniversary`, the billing cycle will be based on the specific date the subscription started (billed fully), while `calendar` sets the billing cycle at the first day of the week/month/year (billed with proration).|
|» coupons|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the coupon.|
|» » code|body|string|true|Unique code used to identify the coupon.|
|» » coupon_type|body|string|false|The type of the coupon. It can have two possible values: `fixed_amount` or `percentage`.<br><br>- If set to `fixed_amount`, the coupon represents a fixed amount discount.<br>- If set to `percentage`, the coupon represents a percentage-based discount.|
|» » amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The amount of the coupon in cents. This field is required only for coupon with `fixed_amount` type.|
|» » amount_currency|body|[CurrencyOrNull](#schemacurrencyornull)|false|The currency of the coupon. This field is required only for coupon with `fixed_amount` type.|
|» » percentage_rate|body|string \| null|false|The percentage rate of the coupon. This field is required only for coupons with a `percentage` coupon type.|
|» » frequency|body|string|false|The frequency of the coupon. It can have three possible values: `once`, `recurring` or `forever`.<br><br>- If set to `once`, the coupon applies to a single invoice.<br>- If set to `recurring`, the coupon applies to the number of billing periods set in `frequency_duration`.<br>- If set to `forever`, the coupon applies to every invoice of the subscription.|
|» » frequency_duration|body|integer \| null|false|Specifies the number of billing periods to which the coupon applies. This field is required only for coupons with a `recurring` frequency type|
|» subscriptions|body|object|false|none|
|» » external_ids|body|[string]|true|none|
|» » plan_code|body|string|false|The code of the plan. It serves as a unique identifier associated with the new plan to which the customer is upgrading or downgrading.|
|» » terminated_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date and time when the subscription is terminated. It should defined in the future.|
|» billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity to which will be associated a customer if the external_id is not provided. If billing_entity_code is not provided, default billing_entity of organization will be used.|

## Retry an invoice payment

<a id="opIdretryPayment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/retry_payment \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "payment_method": {
      "payment_method_type": "provider",
      "payment_method_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/retry_payment`

This endpoint resends an invoice for collection and retry a payment.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "payment_method": {
    "payment_method_type": "provider",
    "payment_method_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retry-an-invoice-payment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|
|body|body|object|false|Payment method to use for the retry (optional)|
|» payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Reference to a specific payment method for processing the payment.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "status": 401,
  "error": "Unauthorized"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "status": 404,
  "error": "Not Found",
  "code": "object_not_found"
}
```

> 405 Response

```json
{
  "status": 405,
  "error": "Method Not Allowed",
  "code": "not_allowed"
}
```

<h3 id="retry-an-invoice-payment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Invoice payment retried|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized error|[ApiErrorUnauthorized](#schemaapierrorunauthorized)|
|404|Not Found|Not Found error|[ApiErrorNotFound](#schemaapierrornotfound)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Not Allowed error|[ApiErrorNotAllowed](#schemaapierrornotallowed)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
bearerAuth
</aside>

## Void an invoice

<a id="opIdvoidInvoice"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/invoices/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90/void \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "generate_credit_note": true,
    "refund_amount": 2000,
    "credit_amount": 1150
  }'
```

`POST /invoices/{lago_id}/void`

This endpoint is used for voiding an invoice.
• When no body parameters are provided, the invoice can be voided only if it is in a `finalized` status and its payment status is NOT `succeeded`.
• When `generate_credit_note` is provided (optionally with `refund_amount` and/or `credit_amount`), this validation is bypassed: the invoice is forcibly voided and a credit note is generated. If the specified refund/credit amounts do not cover the full invoice total, the remainder is issued on a second credit note that is created and immediately voided.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "generate_credit_note": true,
  "refund_amount": 2000,
  "credit_amount": 1150
}
```

<h3 id="void-an-invoice-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the invoice within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the invoice's record within the Lago system.|
|body|body|[InvoiceVoidInput](#schemainvoicevoidinput)|false|Void invoice payload|
|» generate_credit_note|body|boolean|false|Set to `true` to force voiding the invoice and generate a credit note.|
|» refund_amount|body|integer|false|Portion of the invoice amount (in cents) to be refunded to the customer in the generated credit note.|
|» credit_amount|body|integer|false|Portion of the invoice amount (in cents) to be credited to the customer's balance in the generated credit note.|

## List all customer's wallets

<a id="opIdfindAllCustomerWallets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/customers/5eb02857-a71e-4ea2-bcf9-57d3a41bc6ba/wallets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets`

This endpoint is used to list all wallets with prepaid credits of a customer.

<h3 id="list-all-customers-wallets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|page|query|integer|false|Page number. Defaults to 1. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the first page.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Number of records per page. Defaults to 100. The maximum is 200, unless another maximum is configured for your organization. A value above the maximum returns a `422` error with `value_is_out_of_range` on `per_page`. A value that is not a positive integer, such as `0`, returns the default number of records.|
|currency|query|string|false|Filter the results by currency, expressed as an ISO 4217 code.|
|billing_entity_codes[]|query|[string]|false|Filter wallets by billing entity codes.|
|external_customer_id|path|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|

## Create a wallet

<a id="opIdcreateCustomerWallet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/customers/5eb02857-a71e-4ea2-bcf9-57d3a41bc6ba/wallets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "wallet": {
      "name": "Prepaid",
      "code": "prepaid",
      "priority": 50,
      "rate_amount": "1.5",
      "currency": "USD",
      "paid_credits": "20.0",
```

<h3 id="create-a-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_customer_id|path|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|body|body|[WalletCreateInput](#schemawalletcreateinput)|true|Wallet payload|
|» wallet|body|object|true|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet.|
|» » code|body|string \| null|false|The code of the wallet.|
|» » priority|body|integer|false|Wallet priority for ordering when a customer has multiple wallets. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50. Wallets with the same priority are applied by expiration date, soonest first, with wallets without an expiration date last, then by creation date, oldest first.|
|» » rate_amount|body|string|true|The rate of conversion between credits and the amount in the specified currency. It indicates the ratio or factor used to convert credits into the corresponding monetary value in the currency of the transaction.|
|» » currency|body|[Currency](#schemacurrency)|false|The currency of the wallet. Required when the customer has no currency yet. When omitted, the wallet uses the customer's currency. When provided on a customer without a currency, it also sets the customer's currency.|
|» » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits. Required only if there is no granted credits.|
|» » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits. Required only if there is no paid credits.|
|» » external_customer_id|body|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|» » billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity associated with the wallet. If not provided, the customer's billing entity is used.|
|» » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The date and time that determines when the wallet will expire. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs that provide additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will be included in the metadata of wallet transactions generated during the wallet creation process.|
|» » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » value|body|string|false|The corresponding value for the key.|
|» » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered when creating the wallet. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » transaction_priority|body|integer|false|The priority of the wallet transactions triggered when creating the wallet. It drives the order in which credits are consumed. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50.|
|» » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with the wallet. It will be added to invoices generated for wallet top-ups, unless a more specific purchase order number is set on the wallet transaction or recurring transaction rule that triggered the top-up.|
|» » applies_to|body|object \| null|false|Limitations that restrict where the wallet credits apply. They can be set on fee types, on billable metrics, or on both.|
|» » » fee_types|body|[[WalletFeeTypeEnum](#schemawalletfeetypeenum)]|false|An array of fee types to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the fee types in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific fee types only.|
|» » » billable_metric_codes|body|[string]|false|An array of billable metric codes to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the billable metric codes in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific metrics only.|
|» » paid_top_up_min_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The minimum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » paid_top_up_max_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » ignore_paid_top_up_limits_on_creation|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to true, the wallet will ignore paid top-up limits on creation.|
|» » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » recurring_transaction_rules|body|[object]|false|List of recurring transaction rules. Only one recurring rule is allowed per wallet. This is a premium feature, the rules are ignored without a premium license.|
|» » » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits used for recurring top-up.|
|» » » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits used for recurring top-up.|
|» » » grants_target_top_up|body|boolean \| null|false|Applies only to `target` rules. When `true`, the recurring top-up grants free credits to reach the target ongoing balance instead of creating a paid top-up (and bypasses the paid top-up minimum). When `false`, the gap is filled with a paid top-up. `null` for `fixed` rules. Defaults to `false` for target rules when omitted.|
|» » » method|body|string|false|The method used for recurring top-up. Possible values are `fixed` or `target`.|
|» » » trigger|body|string|true|The trigger. Possible values are `interval` or `threshold`.|
|» » » interval|body|string|false|The interval used for recurring top-up. It represents the frequency at which automatic top-up occurs. The interval can be one of the following values: `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual` or `yearly`. Required only when trigger is `interval`.|
|» » » started_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The effective start date for recurring top-ups. This date should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The expiration date and time for this specific recurring transaction rule. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » threshold_credits|body|string|false|The threshold for recurring top-ups is the value at which an automatic top-up is triggered. For example, if this threshold is set at 10 credits, an automatic top-up will occur whenever the wallet balance falls to or below 10 credits. Required only when trigger is set to `threshold`.|
|» » » target_ongoing_balance|body|string|false|The target ongoing balance is the value set for the ongoing balance to be reached by the automatic top-up. Required only when trigger is set to `target`.|
|» » » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs containing additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will populate the metadata of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule.|
|» » » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » » value|body|string|false|The value associated with the key.|
|» » » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with this recurring transaction rule. It will be added to invoices generated for the resulting wallet top-ups. If not set, falls back to the wallet's `purchase_order_number`.|
|» » » ignore_paid_top_up_limits|body|boolean|false|When true, this rule can top up the wallet with transactions that exceed the paid top-up limits. Defaults to false.|
|» » » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing recurring top-up payments.|
|» » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing wallet top-up payments.|
|» » metadata|body|[MetadataInput](#schemametadatainput)|false|Metadata to set as key-value pairs. Keys are strings (max 100 characters), values can be strings (max 255 characters) or null.|

## Retrieve a wallet

<a id="opIdfindCustomerWallet"></a>

`GET /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets/{code}`

This endpoint is used to retrieve an existing wallet with prepaid credits.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_customer_id|path|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|code|path|string|true|A unique wallet identifier within a customer. It is either set by the user at creation or auto-generated by Lago if not provided.|

`PUT /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets/{code}`

This endpoint is used to update an existing wallet with prepaid credits. A terminated wallet cannot be updated and returns a `422` error.

<h3 id="update-a-wallet-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_customer_id|path|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|code|path|string|true|A unique wallet identifier within a customer. It is either set by the user at creation or auto-generated by Lago if not provided.|
|body|body|[WalletUpdateInput](#schemawalletupdateinput)|true|Wallet update payload|
|» wallet|body|object|true|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet.|
|» » code|body|string \| null|false|The code of the wallet.|
|» » priority|body|integer|false|Wallet priority for ordering when a customer has multiple wallets. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50. Wallets with the same priority are applied by expiration date, soonest first, with wallets without an expiration date last, then by creation date, oldest first.|
|» » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The date and time that determines when the wallet will expire. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » paid_top_up_min_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The minimum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » paid_top_up_max_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity associated with the wallet.|
|» » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with the wallet. It will be added to invoices generated for wallet top-ups, unless a more specific purchase order number is set on the wallet transaction or recurring transaction rule that triggered the top-up.|
|» » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » recurring_transaction_rules|body|[object]|false|List of recurring transaction rules. Only one recurring rule is allowed per wallet. This is a premium feature, the rules are ignored without a premium license.|
|» » » lago_id|body|string(uuid)|false|A unique identifier for the recurring transaction rule in the Lago application. Can be used to update a recurring transaction rule.|
|» » » trigger|body|string|true|The trigger. Possible values are `interval` or `threshold`.|
|» » » method|body|string|false|The method used for recurring top-up. Possible values are `fixed` or `target`.|
|» » » interval|body|string|false|The interval used for recurring top-up. It represents the frequency at which automatic top-up occurs. The interval can be one of the following values: `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual` or `yearly`. Required only when trigger is set to `interval`.|
|» » » threshold_credits|body|string|false|The threshold for recurring top-ups is the value at which an automatic top-up is triggered. For example, if this threshold is set at 10 credits, an automatic top-up will occur whenever the wallet balance falls to or below 10 credits. Required only when trigger is set to `threshold`.|
|» » » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits. Required only if there is no granted credits.|
|» » » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits. Required only if there is no paid credits.|
|» » » grants_target_top_up|body|boolean \| null|false|Applies only to `target` rules. When `true`, the recurring top-up grants free credits to reach the target ongoing balance instead of creating a paid top-up (and bypasses the paid top-up minimum). When `false`, the gap is filled with a paid top-up. `null` for `fixed` rules. Defaults to `false` for target rules when omitted.|
|» » » started_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The effective start date for recurring top-ups. This date should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The expiration date and time for this specific recurring transaction rule. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » target_ongoing_balance|body|string|false|The target ongoing balance is the value set for the ongoing balance to be reached by the automatic top-up. Required only when trigger is set to `target`.|
|» » » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs containing additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will populate the metadata of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule.|
|» » » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » » value|body|string|false|The value associated with the key.|
|» » » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with this recurring transaction rule. It will be added to invoices generated for the resulting wallet top-ups. If not set, falls back to the wallet's `purchase_order_number`.|
|» » » ignore_paid_top_up_limits|body|boolean|false|When true, this rule can top up the wallet with transactions that exceed the paid top-up limits. Defaults to false.|
|» » » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing recurring top-up payments.|
|» » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing wallet top-up payments.|
|» » applies_to|body|object \| null|false|Limitations that restrict where the wallet credits apply. They can be set on fee types, on billable metrics, or on both.|
|» » » fee_types|body|[[WalletFeeTypeEnum](#schemawalletfeetypeenum)]|false|An array of fee types to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the fee types in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific fee types only.|
|» » » billable_metric_codes|body|[string]|false|An array of billable metric codes to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the billable metric codes in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific metrics only.|
|» » metadata|body|[MetadataInput](#schemametadatainput)|false|Metadata to set as key-value pairs. Keys are strings (max 100 characters), values can be strings (max 255 characters) or null.|

`POST /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets/{wallet_code}/metadata`

|body|body|[WalletMetadataResponse](#schemawalletmetadataresponse)|true|none|

`POST /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets/{wallet_code}/alerts`

This endpoint allows you to create new alerts for a wallet. Send a single alert object wrapped in `alert` key to create one alert, or an array of alert objects wrapped in `alerts` key to create multiple alerts atomically.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alert": {
    "code": "wallet_balance_alert",
    "name": "Wallet Balance Alert",
    "thresholds": [
      {
        "code": "warn",
        "notify_on": [
          "triggered",
          "resolved"
        ],
        "recurring": false,
        "value": 99
      }
    ],
    "alert_type": "wallet_balance_amount"
  }
}
```

## Update a wallet alert

<a id="opIdupdateCustomerWalletAlert"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/customers/5eb02857-a71e-4ea2-bcf9-57d3a41bc6ba/wallets/wallet-code/alerts/balance_threshold_alert \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "alert": {
      "code": "wallet_balance_alert",
      "name": "Wallet Balance Alert",
      "thresholds": [
        {
          "code": "warn",
          "notify_on": [
            "triggered",
            "resolved"
          ],
          "recurring": false,
          "value": 99
        }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /customers/{external_customer_id}/wallets/{wallet_code}/alerts/{code}`

This endpoint allows you to update an existing alert for a wallet. A non-empty `thresholds` array replaces the whole set of thresholds on the alert. When `thresholds` is left out, or sent as an empty array, the thresholds already on the alert are kept. A threshold sent with a `code` it already had, and without `notify_on`, keeps the `notify_on` it had.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "alert": {
    "code": "wallet_balance_alert",
    "name": "Wallet Balance Alert",
    "thresholds": [
      {
        "code": "warn",
        "notify_on": [
          "triggered",
          "resolved"
        ],
        "recurring": false,
        "value": 99
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-wallet-alert-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|external_customer_id|path|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|wallet_code|path|string|true|A unique wallet identifier within a customer. It is either set by the user at creation or auto-generated by Lago if not provided.|
|code|path|string|true|Unique code of the alert|
|body|body|[WalletAlertUpdateInput](#schemawalletalertupdateinput)|true|Update an existing alert for a wallet|
|» alert|body|object|true|none|
|» » code|body|string|false|Unique code used to identify the alert.|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the alert.|
|» » thresholds|body|[[AlertThresholdInput](#schemaalertthresholdinput)]|false|Array of thresholds associated with the alert. An alert accepts at most 20 thresholds, and a larger array returns a `422` error with `too_many_thresholds` on `thresholds`. Two thresholds cannot share the same value and the same `recurring` flag. The value of a recurring threshold must be positive.|
|» » code|body|string|false|Unique code used to identify the alert.|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the alert.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "alert": {
    "lago_id": "1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90",
```

<h3 id="create-a-wallet-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[WalletCreateInput](#schemawalletcreateinput)|true|Wallet payload|
|» wallet|body|object|true|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet.|
|» » code|body|string \| null|false|The code of the wallet.|
|» » priority|body|integer|false|Wallet priority for ordering when a customer has multiple wallets. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50. Wallets with the same priority are applied by expiration date, soonest first, with wallets without an expiration date last, then by creation date, oldest first.|
|» » rate_amount|body|string|true|The rate of conversion between credits and the amount in the specified currency. It indicates the ratio or factor used to convert credits into the corresponding monetary value in the currency of the transaction.|
|» » currency|body|[Currency](#schemacurrency)|false|The currency of the wallet. Required when the customer has no currency yet. When omitted, the wallet uses the customer's currency. When provided on a customer without a currency, it also sets the customer's currency.|
|» » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits. Required only if there is no granted credits.|
|» » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits. Required only if there is no paid credits.|
|» » external_customer_id|body|string|true|The customer external unique identifier (provided by your own application)|
|» » billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity associated with the wallet. If not provided, the customer's billing entity is used.|
|» » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The date and time that determines when the wallet will expire. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs that provide additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will be included in the metadata of wallet transactions generated during the wallet creation process.|
|» » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » value|body|string|false|The corresponding value for the key.|
|» » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered when creating the wallet. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » transaction_priority|body|integer|false|The priority of the wallet transactions triggered when creating the wallet. It drives the order in which credits are consumed. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50.|
|» » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with the wallet. It will be added to invoices generated for wallet top-ups, unless a more specific purchase order number is set on the wallet transaction or recurring transaction rule that triggered the top-up.|
|» » applies_to|body|object \| null|false|Limitations that restrict where the wallet credits apply. They can be set on fee types, on billable metrics, or on both.|
|» » » fee_types|body|[[WalletFeeTypeEnum](#schemawalletfeetypeenum)]|false|An array of fee types to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the fee types in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific fee types only.|
|» » » billable_metric_codes|body|[string]|false|An array of billable metric codes to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the billable metric codes in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific metrics only.|
|» » paid_top_up_min_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The minimum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » paid_top_up_max_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » ignore_paid_top_up_limits_on_creation|body|boolean \| null|false|If set to true, the wallet will ignore paid top-up limits on creation.|
|» » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » recurring_transaction_rules|body|[object]|false|List of recurring transaction rules. Only one recurring rule is allowed per wallet. This is a premium feature, the rules are ignored without a premium license.|
|» » » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits used for recurring top-up.|
|» » » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits used for recurring top-up.|
|» » » grants_target_top_up|body|boolean \| null|false|Applies only to `target` rules. When `true`, the recurring top-up grants free credits to reach the target ongoing balance instead of creating a paid top-up (and bypasses the paid top-up minimum). When `false`, the gap is filled with a paid top-up. `null` for `fixed` rules. Defaults to `false` for target rules when omitted.|
|» » » method|body|string|false|The method used for recurring top-up. Possible values are `fixed` or `target`.|
|» » » trigger|body|string|true|The trigger. Possible values are `interval` or `threshold`.|
|» » » interval|body|string|false|The interval used for recurring top-up. It represents the frequency at which automatic top-up occurs. The interval can be one of the following values: `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual` or `yearly`. Required only when trigger is `interval`.|
|» » » started_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The effective start date for recurring top-ups. This date should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The expiration date and time for this specific recurring transaction rule. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » threshold_credits|body|string|false|The threshold for recurring top-ups is the value at which an automatic top-up is triggered. For example, if this threshold is set at 10 credits, an automatic top-up will occur whenever the wallet balance falls to or below 10 credits. Required only when trigger is set to `threshold`.|
|» » » target_ongoing_balance|body|string|false|The target ongoing balance is the value set for the ongoing balance to be reached by the automatic top-up. Required only when trigger is set to `target`.|
|» » » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs containing additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will populate the metadata of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule.|
|» » » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » » value|body|string|false|The value associated with the key.|
|» » » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with this recurring transaction rule. It will be added to invoices generated for the resulting wallet top-ups. If not set, falls back to the wallet's `purchase_order_number`.|
|» » » ignore_paid_top_up_limits|body|boolean|false|When true, this rule can top up the wallet with transactions that exceed the paid top-up limits. Defaults to false.|
|» » » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing recurring top-up payments.|
|» » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing wallet top-up payments.|
|» » metadata|body|[MetadataInput](#schemametadatainput)|false|Metadata to set as key-value pairs. Keys are strings (max 100 characters), values can be strings (max 255 characters) or null.|

## Retrieve a wallet

<a id="opIdfindWallet"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.getlago.com/api/v1/wallets/1a901a90-1a90-1a90-1a90-1a901a901a90 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /wallets/{lago_id}`

This endpoint is used to retrieve an existing wallet with prepaid credits.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-wallet-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the wallet within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the wallet's record within the Lago system.|

<h3 id="update-a-wallet-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|lago_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Unique identifier assigned to the wallet within the Lago application. This ID is exclusively created by Lago and serves as a unique identifier for the wallet's record within the Lago system.|
|body|body|[WalletUpdateInput](#schemawalletupdateinput)|true|Wallet update payload|
|» wallet|body|object|true|none|
|» » name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet.|
|» » code|body|string \| null|false|The code of the wallet.|
|» » priority|body|integer|false|Wallet priority for ordering when a customer has multiple wallets. Allowed values: 1-50, where 1 is highest priority and 50 is lowest. Defaults to 50. Wallets with the same priority are applied by expiration date, soonest first, with wallets without an expiration date last, then by creation date, oldest first.|
|» » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The date and time that determines when the wallet will expire. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » paid_top_up_min_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The minimum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » paid_top_up_max_amount_cents|body|integer \| null|false|The maximum amount, in cents, of a single paid top-up transaction.|
|» » billing_entity_code|body|string|false|The code of the billing entity associated with the wallet.|
|» » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with the wallet. It will be added to invoices generated for wallet top-ups, unless a more specific purchase order number is set on the wallet transaction or recurring transaction rule that triggered the top-up.|
|» » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » recurring_transaction_rules|body|[object]|false|List of recurring transaction rules. Only one recurring rule is allowed per wallet. This is a premium feature, the rules are ignored without a premium license.|
|» » » lago_id|body|string(uuid)|false|A unique identifier for the recurring transaction rule in the Lago application. Can be used to update a recurring transaction rule.|
|» » » trigger|body|string|true|The trigger. Possible values are `interval` or `threshold`.|
|» » » method|body|string|false|The method used for recurring top-up. Possible values are `fixed` or `target`.|
|» » » interval|body|string|false|The interval used for recurring top-up. It represents the frequency at which automatic top-up occurs. The interval can be one of the following values: `weekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `semiannual` or `yearly`. Required only when trigger is set to `interval`.|
|» » » threshold_credits|body|string|false|The threshold for recurring top-ups is the value at which an automatic top-up is triggered. For example, if this threshold is set at 10 credits, an automatic top-up will occur whenever the wallet balance falls to or below 10 credits. Required only when trigger is set to `threshold`.|
|» » » paid_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of paid credits. Required only if there is no granted credits.|
|» » » granted_credits|body|string \| null|false|The number of free granted credits. Required only if there is no paid credits.|
|» » » grants_target_top_up|body|boolean \| null|false|Applies only to `target` rules. When `true`, the recurring top-up grants free credits to reach the target ongoing balance instead of creating a paid top-up (and bypasses the paid top-up minimum). When `false`, the gap is filled with a paid top-up. `null` for `fixed` rules. Defaults to `false` for target rules when omitted.|
|» » » started_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The effective start date for recurring top-ups. This date should be provided in ISO 8601 datetime format and expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » expiration_at|body|string \| null(date-time)|false|The expiration date and time for this specific recurring transaction rule. It follows the ISO 8601 datetime format and is expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).|
|» » » target_ongoing_balance|body|string|false|The target ongoing balance is the value set for the ongoing balance to be reached by the automatic top-up. Required only when trigger is set to `target`.|
|» » » invoice_requires_successful_payment|body|boolean|false|A boolean setting that, when set to true, delays issuing an invoice for a wallet top-up until a successful payment is made; if false, the invoice is issued immediately upon wallet top-up, regardless of the payment status. Default value of false.|
|» » » transaction_metadata|body|[object]|false|This optional field allows you to store a list of key-value pairs containing additional information or custom attributes. These key-value pairs will populate the metadata of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule.|
|» » » » key|body|string|false|The unique identifier for the attribute.|
|» » » » value|body|string|false|The value associated with the key.|
|» » » transaction_name|body|string \| null|false|The name of the wallet transactions triggered by this rule. It will appear on the invoice as the label for the fee. If not set, the label on the invoice will fallback to either `Prepaid credits - {{wallet_name}}` if the wallet name is set, or `Prepaid credits`.|
|» » » purchase_order_number|body|string \| null|false|The purchase order number associated with this recurring transaction rule. It will be added to invoices generated for the resulting wallet top-ups. If not set, falls back to the wallet's `purchase_order_number`.|
|» » » ignore_paid_top_up_limits|body|boolean|false|When true, this rule can top up the wallet with transactions that exceed the paid top-up limits. Defaults to false.|
|» » » invoice_custom_section|body|[InvoiceCustomSectionInput](#schemainvoicecustomsectioninput)|false|Configuration for invoice custom sections to apply to invoices generated by this resource.|
|» » » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing recurring top-up payments.|
|» » payment_method|body|[PaymentMethodReference](#schemapaymentmethodreference)|false|Optional payment method to use for processing wallet top-up payments.|
|» » applies_to|body|object \| null|false|Limitations that restrict where the wallet credits apply. They can be set on fee types, on billable metrics, or on both.|
|» » » fee_types|body|[[WalletFeeTypeEnum](#schemawalletfeetypeenum)]|false|An array of fee types to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the fee types in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific fee types only.|
|» » » billable_metric_codes|body|[string]|false|An array of billable metric codes to which the wallet is applicable. By specifying the billable metric codes in this field, you can restrict the wallet's usage to specific metrics only.|
|» » metadata|body|[MetadataInput](#schemametadatainput)|false|Metadata to set as key-value pairs. Keys are strings (max 100 characters), values can be strings (max 255 characters) or null.|
